Solar Words, Straight #4: Energy Cost Recovery. The line on your Hawaiian Electric bill that's behind most of this year's increase. Sources on the last slide.

Follow for more plain-English Oʻahu solar math.

#Oahu #HawaiiSolar #SolarPower #HawaiianElectric #Honolulu

slides.text: The biggest line on your HECO bill pays for fuel and purchased power.
slides.sub: Solar Words, Straight #4: Energy Cost Recovery

slides.label: of a typical Oʻahu bill in November 2026 was the Energy Cost Recovery charge: what HECO pays for fuel and for power it buys from other producers.

slides.text: Same 500 kWh. The energy cost line did the climbing.

chart.note: Typical 500 kWh Oʻahu residential bill, from Hawaiian Electric's monthly filings.

slides.sub: Oʻahu still makes much of its power from imported oil. HECO passes fuel and purchased-power costs through and resets this charge monthly. It says it makes no profit on fuel.

slides.text: Oil jumped this spring. Bills followed weeks later.
slides.sub: HECO says there's typically a 45 to 60 day lag between global oil prices and customer bills.

slides.text: This is why the solar math changed in 2026.
slides.sub: Every kWh your panels cover is a kWh you don't pay the Energy Cost Recovery charge on.
